svg.title: What runs where
svg.desc: Everything runs in one Kubernetes cluster (locally Docker Desktop, k3s in production). In the namespace product-management: the gateway Deployment (2 to 6 pods, autoscaled at 70 percent CPU) behind the Service gateway on port 8080, a LoadBalancer locally and behind an Ingress with TLS in staging and production; a NetworkPolicy lets only the gateway reach the web Deployment (2 pods, Service web) and the api Deployment (2 to 8 pods, autoscaled at 60 percent), whose only Service is the headless Service api. The API connects to postgres.infra.svc.cluster.local:5432 and redis.infra.svc.cluster.local:6379. Secrets database-credentials (made by create-database.sh), redis-credentials (a copy of infra/redis-auth) and api-secrets (signing key, consumers). In the namespace infra, shared by every service: the postgres StatefulSet (PostgreSQL 18) with the volume data-postgres-0 behind Service postgres; the nightly CronJob postgres-backup writing to the volume postgres-backups; the redis Deployment (Redis 8, a pure cache, no volume) behind Service redis; Alloy, which reads every pod log and takes the browser errors on Service alloy-faro; Loki (StatefulSet, volume data-loki-0, 14 days); and Grafana (dashboards and 12 alert rules). In kube-system: metrics-server. In production, nodes added with deploy/scripts/add-node.sh can carry the roles database, cache and apps. Outside the cluster only the browser and the CI/CD pipeline, which reaches the cluster with kubectl through the GitLab agent or a KUBECONFIG.
svg.text: all of it in one Kubernetes cluster
kubectl through the GitLab agent or a KUBECONFIG
